Save and restore the layout, backup folder, sync between phones

This is not a MetroWin layout file
Battery and log reports, saved as text files
The files can hold private things: names, notifications, addresses, what the other apps wrote in the log. Look at a file before you send it to anyone.
Android gives the system dumps and the log of the whole phone only through adb. From a computer, with the phone connected:
The dumps of the battery need it too: allow MetroWin in the screen that opens.
The battery and the power saving now, the standby bucket, the CPU and memory of the process, how it was stopped before, what the launcher has on, and the statistics of Android for this app.
Battery state of the whole phone
The battery now and the statistics of Android for every app: consumption, wakelocks, alarms, screen. It can take a few seconds.
System log of the whole phone
Everything Android has in its log buffers now, from every app. Without the READ_LOGS permission it holds only the lines of this app.
Everything this app wrote in the log since it was started, as far as the buffers of Android still have it (they are circular: the file says from when it starts).

The tile of an app turns over to show what its notifications say: messages, pictures, the song that plays. Anyone who sees your screen sees it too, so it is off until you turn it on. Choose what shows in the live tiles page.

No city found with that name
Could not search. Is there a connection?
Could not find where you are
Weather comes from Open-Meteo and is fetched when the launcher opens, at most every half hour. The city is the only thing sent.
Choose a city to see the weather here and on the tile.
add a contact, a website or a widget
That does not look like a web address.
This phone has no widgets to add.
What you type in the app list is also looked for in these. The web search opens DuckDuckGo in your browser; nothing is sent until you touch it.
Choose what each gesture does. A double tap waits a moment before a single tap is understood, only while one is set.

The swipe up and hold of Android\'s gesture navigation is handled by the system, not by the launcher. With a launcher that is not the phone\'s own, many phones make you hold the swipe for a second or more, or are slow to open the recent apps, and the launcher cannot change that.

What opens them at once: the gesture “open the recent apps” above, the Recent apps button among the Action Center toggles, the Quick Settings tile (pull down the panel from any app), or the 3-button navigation of Android, where the Recents button has no wait. All but the last need the screen lock service below.
add the tile to Quick Settings
On: the launcher can lock the screen and open the recent apps
Off: locking the screen and the recent apps button need it

Android only lets an app lock the screen or open the recent apps through an accessibility service. This one does nothing else: it reads nothing from the screen and asks for no events. The recent apps open at once, without the wait that the swipe of Android\'s gesture navigation can have with a launcher that is not the phone\'s own.
Turn on the screen lock service in the accessibility settings first

Lets the MetroWin launcher lock the screen, open the recent apps, take a screenshot, open the power menu or split the screen when you choose that for a gesture or a button. If you turn on the Action Center over other apps, it also holds a thin strip at the top edge of the screen that waits for a swipe down. It does not read or change anything on the screen.

Choose any folder, also one of Google Drive or another cloud app that shows in the file picker. The layout is saved there as metrowin-layout.json when the launcher goes to the background, no more often than you choose.
There is no backup in that folder
Work profile and private space: pause them, show or hide their apps
show its apps in the app list
This phone has no work profile or private space.
A paused profile runs nothing and its apps cannot be opened until it is resumed. Android asks for your authentication to unlock the private space.
Try “open Maps”, “call Anna”, “turn on the torch”, “search for pizza”
I could not find “%1$s” on this phone
Speech recognition is not available on this phone.
Allow the microphone to talk to the launcher.
Speech recognition needs a connection for this language.
Speech recognition is busy. Try again in a moment.
Speak to the launcher: open apps, call, search, torch
Shows a microphone in the search box of the app list.
Uses the offline voice model when the phone has one for your language. Otherwise your voice goes to the speech service you chose in Android.

“Call Anna” places the call without opening the dialer first. Off, the dialer opens with the number written in, one tap from calling, so a word heard wrong does not call anyone. Android asks for the phone permission the first time.
“call Anna” opens the dialer with her number, or calls her if you turned on “call at once”
“search for pizza recipes”, or just say what you want to know
“turn on the torch”, “turn off the torch”
You can also start it with a double tap or a two-finger swipe: choose “voice” in Gestures.
Rotation, how apps open, refresh rate, language of the launcher
In landscape the Start screen fits more columns of tiles. “Follow the phone” respects the rotation lock of Android.

Asks the screen for its fastest mode (120 Hz and more) at the current resolution, but only while you use it: three seconds after the last touch it asks for 60 Hz, the slowest rate that still looks smooth. Turn it off to let Android decide always.
Icon packs and theme files you can share
No icon pack is installed. Packs made for ADW, Nova, Apex or Go Launcher work here.
A pack replaces the icons of the apps it has an icon for. The Metro apps of the phone keep their glyphs.
Saves the colours, the dark or light mode, the clock, the tile size and the icon pack in a small file to share.
Applies a theme file. Your tiles and your other settings stay as they are.
That file is not a theme of this launcher
The Metro lock screen: photo, clock, alarm, notifications
Without its own photo the lock screen uses the Start photo, and black without that.
use the photo on the phone\'s lock screen
Sets the photo as the wallpaper of the Android lock screen.
Could not set the lock screen photo
Choose a photo first, or set a Start photo

Android does not let a launcher replace its lock screen. The Metro lock screen runs as the screen saver instead: pick “Metro lock screen” there, and it shows while the phone charges or rests on a dock. Swipe it up to leave.
expand: the tile grows into the app
Expand keeps the Start screen still and grows the app out of the tile you touched (on the list, out of the middle). Reduce motion in Accessibility turns both off.
Choose a backup folder first: the sync file lives in it. A folder in a cloud app (Google Drive, for example) syncs your phones.

Use the same passphrase on every phone. The file is encrypted with it (AES-256) before it goes in the folder. The passphrase stays on this phone and is never written to the folder: if you lose it, the synced data cannot be read.
Turn sync on, choose a folder and a passphrase first
Synced: this phone\'s Start is in the folder
Synced: Start updated from the folder
Both phones changed. This one was kept; the other one is saved in the folder as %1$s
Wrong passphrase for the file in the folder
The sync file in the folder is damaged or is not ours

The first sync of a phone that finds a file in the folder takes it, and keeps what it had as the backup file in the folder. After that, whatever changed since the last sync goes across; if both phones changed, this one wins and the other is kept as a separate file.
Shows a “reply” link on messages that can be answered, and sends your answer to the app that posted it.
An app with several notifications shows as one line you can open. Swiping it away clears them all.
let apps publish their own tile text
An app that asks for the permission can put a title, a line of text and a number on its own tile, like a Windows Phone live tile. Only its own tile: the launcher knows who is asking.
No app has published a tile yet.
put live content on its own tile in MetroWin Launcher
Lets the app show a title, a line of text and a number on its own tile on the Start screen.
Text size and weight, less motion, stronger contrast, TalkBack
Screens fade instead of swinging, tiles stop flipping and tilting, and apps open without an animation. It is also on whenever Android\'s animations are removed.
Tiles get a white frame and stay solid over a Start photo, and grey text turns to full colour.

Every tile says what it is, and its notifications. In the TalkBack actions menu a tile offers: unpin, change size, move earlier, move later (folders: rename, take apart). The app list reads each app and offers its menu.
So that pressing Home brings you here. Android asks you to confirm.
Finds the weather where you are. Used once, when you ask for it: you can also type a city.
Lets you talk to the launcher. It listens only while the listening screen is open.
Shows your notifications in the Action Center and the counters on the tiles. Android has a settings page for it.
Lets a gesture lock the screen. It reads nothing from the screen. Turn it on in the accessibility settings.
Stops Android from closing the launcher to save battery.
The tour of the launcher, with the permissions it can ask for.

MetroWin Launcher turns your phone into a Windows Phone Start screen. This short tour shows how to use it, and asks for a few permissions one at a time, only when a feature needs them. Every one of them is optional.
Swipe left, or use the buttons below, to go on.
Leave at any time with “skip”. You can see the tour again from Launcher settings → tools → about.
Android opens its Home app every time you press Home. For MetroWin to be what you see, it has to be that app.
Press Home at any time to come back to Start.
If Android asks which launcher to use, choose MetroWin Launcher and “always”.
Tiles are your apps and live information, laid out the way you like.
Tap a tile to open it. Touch and hold to edit: remove it, change its size, or drag it somewhere else.
Drop a tile on the middle of another one to make a folder, or hold a tile, touch the folder button and pick several tiles at once. A folder opens in place.
The arrow after the last tile goes to the next Start screen (you can have three), then to the app list.
In edit mode, “+” adds a contact, a website or a widget to Start.
Make a tile small and drag other small tiles to the empty squares beside it: that is a group, without a folder.
Some tiles show what is happening: your latest photos, your next appointment, the faces of your contacts, your missed calls. The information never leaves your phone.
Tiles flip by themselves, each one at its own time.
In edit mode, choose a tile\'s style: standard, Iconic (a big number) or Cycle (photos).
The Weather tile shows the forecast of a city. It asks Open-Meteo, an open service, over the internet. Nothing else leaves your phone.
Choose the city in Launcher settings → live tiles: by name, or with your location.
Tap the tile for the forecast of the next days.
Swipe left from Start, or use the arrow, to see every app in alphabetical order.
Touch a letter to jump to another one. The star takes you to the app you opened last.
Type in the search box to find apps, contacts and Android settings, or to search the web.
Touch and hold an app to pin it to Start, hide it or uninstall it.
Or say it: tap the microphone in the search box and try “open Maps” or “call Anna”.
Pull down from the very top edge of the screen, on any page, to open it.
Four quick buttons on top, and an arrow for the rest. The torch really switches on; the others open the right screen of Android.
Swipe a notification to the right to dismiss it. When the app allows it you can reply from here, and several notifications of one app are grouped.
Drag the panel back up, or press Back, to close it.
Everything follows your finger. A few gestures can do what you choose in Launcher settings → gestures.
On Start, swipe from the right edge to go on to the app list, and from the left edge to go back.
Double tap the background of Start, or swipe down or up with two fingers, to lock the screen, switch on the torch, speak, search…
Back goes back one layer at a time, and the system gesture moves the screen with your finger.
To save battery, Android can close apps in the background. If it closes the launcher, the counters, the Action Center and the sync stop until you open it again.
Allow MetroWin Launcher not to be limited by battery optimization, and it stays alive.
Some phones (Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo, Samsung…) also have their own “autostart” or “protected apps” list in their settings: add MetroWin Launcher there too.

Open Launcher settings in the app list, or tap the Launcher button of the Action Center. Each section is a page, in four groups: look, behavior, apps and tools. The search box on top finds any setting and takes you to it.

look: start+theme (theme, light or dark, OLED black, accent colors, Start photo), start screen (tiles, clock, number of Start screens), icons & themes, accessibility (text size, bold text, less motion, more contrast, TalkBack) and the lock screen.
behavior: screen+language (rotation, how apps open, 120 Hz, language), gestures (every swipe, tap and edge pull, the recent apps too), notifications+actions (the Action Center), voice and battery.

apps: the app list (the groups at the top, hidden, renamed and locked apps), search (what the box looks in, what it answers, the web engine), live tiles (the weather city, WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram…) and profiles (work, private space).

tools: backup+sync (a file or a folder, and an encrypted sync between your phones), kid\'s corner (Start with only the apps you choose) and about (the version, and this tour whenever you want it again).
Lost? The box at the top of the settings finds any setting by its name or by what it is for, and takes you to it. The search of the app list finds them too.
Make a folder with several tiles
Touch the tiles to put in the folder
Touch more tiles to add them to the folder
Flat Windows Phone tiles, as ever.
Frosted, rounded glass over a glowing backdrop.
Material You: soft shapes and colors that follow your wallpaper.
use the colors of the wallpaper
Android 12 and later give every app the colors of your wallpaper. Turn it off to build the theme from the accent color you choose below.
Make any color: hue, strength and lightness.
Three themes and any color. Open Launcher settings → start+theme to choose.
Classic is the flat Windows Phone look. Modern Glass is frosted glass over a glowing backdrop. Modern Droid follows Material You.
Pick one of the 20 accent colors, or make your own with the three sliders. Dark, light, or by the hour, in every theme.
Power saving, and what the launcher does when it is not on screen
Saves when Android\'s battery saver is on, or when the battery is at 20% or less and the phone is not charging.
Never saves: tiles keep flipping and the screen is asked for its fastest refresh rate.
Tiles stop flipping by themselves and photos stop cycling.
The 120 Hz request is dropped: the phone picks its own refresh rate.
Weather, contacts, calendar and photos are read less often, and the sync waits longer.
With another app on screen, or with the screen off, the launcher does nothing: no timers, no listeners, no refresh. What changed in the meantime is read once, when you come back.

Contacts, calendar, photos and calls are read only for the live tiles you pinned to Start, each at its own pace: the next event and the missed calls every two minutes at most, photos every quarter of an hour, faces every half hour, birthdays every twelve hours. The weather waits ten minutes after a try, with or without a connection.
The lock screen service asks Android for no events, so it never wakes the launcher when you switch apps.

Notifications: Android still tells the service when one arrives, but the launcher reads none of them until it is on screen, however many come. The same goes for the list of apps when they are updated. Everything is read once when you come back; with the launcher open, a burst is read no more than twice a second.
It costs almost no battery: off screen, or with another app in front, the launcher reads nothing and runs no timers.
For OLED screens: in the dark theme the backgrounds are pure black, so those pixels are off. More contrast and less battery. It does nothing in the light theme.
Have an OLED screen? Turn on “OLED black” in start+theme for a pure black background.

With notification access and the switch “live content of other apps” in the notifications page, the tile of WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Reddit or any other app turns over to show what is going on in it: who wrote and what, a picture, the song that plays, a download. Everything comes from the notifications; nothing leaves the phone.
Off now: turn on notification access and the switch “live content of other apps” in the notifications page.
A face for each chat, with who wrote, the last line and the picture of the sender; the other notifications (a like, a reply) as a title and a line. The counter adds up the messages, one by one.
Only who wrote or which app it is from: the text of messages and notifications stays off the tiles, for anyone who sees your screen.
A notification with a picture shows it on the tile.
The song, the artist and the cover, on the tile of the app that plays and on the Music tile.
What an app is downloading, uploading or syncing, with how far along it is.
No app has live content now.
Switch an app off and its tile stays as it is. The apps appear here once they have something to show.
The same switch as in the notifications page. It puts the text of your messages on Start, so it stays off until you turn it on.
Android asks for it in its own screen: the launcher only reads the notifications that are already up.
Nothing yet. Once the switch and the notification access are on, the apps that have notifications up are listed here with what was found in them.
If an app shows nothing on its tile, look here: if it is listed, the tile can show it; if it is not, the app wrote nothing the launcher can read.
stop asking for the screen lock
Set a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password) in Android first: there is nothing to ask for without it.
The apps you open most from the launcher, in a group at the top of the list. The counts stay on this phone and are not part of the backups.
The apps installed in the last week, at the top of the list. Right after setting up or restoring a phone nothing is called new.
Chips under the search box that show only the apps of one kind. Only the apps that say what they are (games, social, music…) are in them.
No renamed apps. Press and hold an app in the list and choose “rename”.
Touch an app to give it back its own name.
No locked apps. Press and hold an app in the list and choose “ask for the screen lock”.
Touch an app to stop asking. The lock is for opening from the launcher (list, tiles, search, voice): an app can still be opened from a notification, from the recent apps or from another app.
Done: look in the clock app
No clock app can set it on this phone
Sums (12*3+4, 15% of 80), conversions (5 km in miles, 30 c in f), phone numbers, links and email addresses, and timers and alarms (“timer 10 minutes”, “alarm at 7:30”). All worked out on the phone.
The last searches are offered when you touch the search box. They stay on this phone and are not part of the backups.
put an Android setting on Start
No number to call was picked.
pull down the Android quick settings
No app chosen for this gesture: choose one in the gestures page.
Allow the brightness slider (Android asks in its own screen)
volume and brightness in the Action Center
Two sliders and the sound, vibration and silent buttons. The volume needs no permission; the brightness needs the “modify system settings” access, which you give in a screen of Android.
A touch on the time of Start opens the clock, on the date the calendar.
week number next to the date
Makes the text of the whole launcher smaller or bigger, from 85% to 130%.
More room for Start. A swipe from the top edge shows the bar for a moment; with the bar hidden, that swipe is the system\'s, so open the Action Center with a gesture of the gestures page instead.
Zoom in on the part of the photo you like: the point you choose with the two position sliders stays in view.
what do you count? (glasses of water…)
The name of the app under its tile. Off, the tiles are only their pictures.
Puts back the tiles Start had when you installed the launcher, and takes away the ones you added (contacts, sites, notes, widgets…). Undo brings back everything but the widgets.
“100 usd in eur”, “50 dollars in euros”. Asks api.frankfurter.dev (the rates of the European Central Bank) once in a while; it sends nothing you type. Off until you turn it on.
Events of the next six months whose title matches. Needs the calendar permission; it is read on the phone and nothing leaves it.
Smaller squares and tighter rows: more apps on the screen.
To change the brightness, allow “modify system settings” for the launcher in the screen that just opened.
Silent mode needs the “do not disturb” access: allow it for the launcher in the screen that just opened.
“turn up the volume”, “volume at 50 percent”, “brightness to the maximum”
“navigate to Rome”, “take me to the station”
“text Anna I’m late” (it opens the message for you to send), “send a message to Marco saying hello”
Allow the launcher in this screen and the button switches quiet hours at once.
Follows the sunrise and sunset of the weather’s city (the weather has to have loaded once). Until then, and when it cannot know them, the hours below are used.
Makes all the text of the launcher heavier. The bold text of Android turns it on too.
Uses the font of Android instead of the one the look brings.
Android 13 and later. The first choice follows the language of the phone.
The weather the weather tile fetched last. Nothing is fetched by the lock screen.
The next event of your calendar in the next 24 hours. Needs the calendar permission. Anyone who sees the screen can read it.
Tiles, clock and date, number of Start screens, status bar
What the search box looks in, answers and remembers
Finds the settings of the launcher by name or by what they are for, and opens the page where each one is.
The words of notes and lists, countdowns, counters and the names of sites pinned to Start.
slide: the new face slides in
mixed: each tile in its own way
Scan a code or a text
Rings when a timer of Start ends.
Tells you what you asked to be reminded of.
The timer is one alarm of Android: nothing runs in the background while it counts, and the numbers move only while this page is on screen.
No headlines yet. They are read when the launcher is on screen and there is a connection.
Nothing to show yet. The rates are read when the launcher is on screen and there is a connection.
Currencies: European Central Bank rates through api.frankfurter.dev. Coins: CoinGecko.
What should I remind you of?
Nothing to remember. Write what, and choose when.
Android does not let the launcher ring to the minute: a reminder can be a few minutes late.
No favourite yet. Star a contact and it appears here.
To show your favourites the launcher needs to read the contacts.
To show the latest calls the launcher needs to read the call log.
Where the accent colour is used
Where a part is off, the colour is a grey that suits the theme.
How the photo fills the screen
A chime for a new notification and a short glide when the Action Center comes down or goes, also over other apps. They follow the volume of the phone.
A touch starts the navigation in Google Maps.
To show the photos of an album the launcher needs to read the photos.
No group found. Make a label in your contacts and it shows here.
To show the people of a group the launcher needs to read the contacts.
Slide brings the new face in from below; mixed uses one way on some tiles and the other on the rest. Nothing moves by itself while saving the battery or with reduced motion.
A feed of your own (RSS or Atom)
Not a good address: it must be a web page on the Internet, over https.

The most important stories of the day, in the language and the country of the phone. They are asked for only while the News tile is on Start and the launcher is on screen: at most every half hour, every three hours when saving the battery.
Currencies come from the European Central Bank (api.frankfurter.dev), coins from CoinGecko. There are no stock prices: no free source gives them without an account.
A large title (start, apps) behind the pages, which moves slower than the page when it slides. Off until you ask for it.
At the bottom while you edit the tiles: the … button shows the names of the buttons.
Up to five apps with the number of their notifications, under the time. If you do not choose, the apps with the most notifications.
The last notification of this app, written out (who and what) on the lock screen. Anyone who sees the screen reads it.
While a song plays: its cover, its name and the buttons to skip and pause.

The volume keys draw a Metro panel over the launcher for what is sounding now: the call, the music (with the name of the app) or the ringer. Android does not let an app lower the volume of another app by itself; for a player that has a volume of its own (a cast, a speaker) the panel moves that one.

The same banner over the app you are in, when the launcher is not on screen. Not on the lock screen, not for silent notifications, not when Do Not Disturb blocks them. Android\'s own banner still shows. Choose the apps with the banner switch of each app.

Every notification that arrives goes from the shade of Android to the Action Center: the quiet ones, those that come with the screen off or locked, and those already there when you turn this on. Calls, alarms, music and anything ongoing stay where they are, and so do the apps you keep out of the Action Center. It stays in the Action Center until you dismiss it. Android shows its own for an instant first and the app makes its sound: neither can be stopped. The app is told the notification was dismissed.

A swipe down from the very top edge of the screen (a thin strip, 20 dp) opens the Action Center of the launcher over the app you are in. It needs the screen lock service in the accessibility settings, the only kind of window that can be over the status bar. A touch on the strip does nothing, and the panel of Android stays reachable from just below it. Not on the lock screen.
Needs \"Display over other apps\" for MetroWin: turn the switch on to allow it.
A Metro banner at the top while the launcher is on screen. The banner of Android may show too: turn it off for an app in the notification settings of that app.
Choose for each app where its notifications show: the Action Center, the lock screen, the banner. The sound is Android\'s: the page of each app opens from here.
Reminders, events (Google Calendar), notes (Google Keep), places near you (Google Maps), codes and text (Google Lens): “remind me to call Anna tomorrow at 6”, “pharmacy near me”.
Digits find the contacts by the letters on the keys (266 is Ann…) and by their number.
Above the search box: the date, the next event, the weather and the reminders.
Android moves the volume of all the media together: it cannot lower a single app.
show the names of the buttons
hide the names of the buttons
The step counter of the phone needs the permission for physical activity. Nothing leaves the phone.
Counted by the step sensor of the phone, from the first time the tile read it today.
The recorder needs the permission to use the microphone. Recordings stay in the storage of the app.
The microphone could not be opened. Is a call going on?
No cards yet. Add a loyalty card or a ticket with the number under its barcode.
The name is empty or the number cannot be drawn: letters, digits and signs only.

The position could not be found. Is the location on?
That is not a web address
Second time zone under the date

Choose the kinds of file the search looks for by name. Each one asks for its permission; the names are read on the phone and nothing leaves it. From Android 13 the phone shows documents only to the app that made them, so Documents may find nothing there.
Save the list of my apps
Writes the names of the apps you installed to a file. Nothing else leaves the phone.
Set up from a list of apps
Reads a saved list and shows the apps this phone does not have; each one opens its page in the store, where you install it.
That file is not a list of apps
Missing on this phone: %d (touch one to open the store)
Title of a group of tiles
Title of the group that starts here (empty for none)
Offers the Large size (four tiles across and four down) in the edit bar and the resize arrow. Tiles already large stay large.
Shows the titles written above groups of tiles, and starts each group on a row of its own. Off: Start is one plain grid; the titles are kept.
Offers the collage (many small pictures side by side) to the tiles that have photos.
A wide Calendar tile lists the next events; a large one shows the month and the next events.
Time left on the Battery tile
Says how long the charge should last, as Android predicts it (Android 12 and later).
Previous, play or pause and next, on the Music tile while something plays. They need the notification access.
Keep the Start screens under a name (Home, Work, Travel) and put one back with a touch. Putting a layout on first saves what is on Start into the layout that was on.
Each layout with an hour takes Start over at that hour, once. One you choose by hand stays until the next hour comes.
A photo for each Start screen
Each Start screen can have its own photo. One without shows the photo chosen for all.
App silenced for now. Its notifications come back when the time is up.
Silence an app from the panel
A long press on a notification offers to silence its app for an hour, eight hours or until morning: its notifications and banners stay out of sight and come back when the time is up.
In the Action Center the messages and the calls come before the other notifications.
Leave out notifications with some words

A notification that has one of the words below is taken away from Android and shown nowhere: not in the Action Center, not as a banner, not on the lock screen. Calls, alarms and music are never touched.
A word or a piece of one
Length of the timed quiet mode
100% is as designed; 200% is twice as fast. The springs (the bounce of a tile) keep their own pace.
How far a tile or a button leans away from the finger. 0% keeps only the sinking. It is the press of the Classic look.
Strength of the vibration of a tap
Also looks in the notifications that wait in the Action Center. They are read on the phone, only while you search.
A word and a colon in front narrow the search: app:, contact:, setting:, file:, event:, notif:, tile:, web: (or a:, c:, s:, f:, e:, n:, t:, w:).
Model, Android, memory, space and how long the phone has been on, on this page. Nothing leaves the phone.
Each backup is also kept under the minute it was made, and the oldest ones go once there are more than this. Touch one below to put it back.
Sends the Start screens, the shortcuts and the settings, as a file, to the app or the person you choose. Nothing of this phone alone goes in it (no passphrase, no folder).
Choose the parts of the backup to put in place of what is on the phone now.

Volume presets in the Action Center

Save the volumes as they are now

Switches and sound modes by name

string-array.name: tips
string-array.item: Press and hold a tile to move it, make it bigger or smaller, or take it off Start.
Press and hold an empty place on Start to add a tile: contacts, notes, timers, the weather and many more.
Pull down from the top of the screen to open the Action Center.
Type a sum like 12*3+4 in the search box and the answer is there.
Put app: or contact: before a word in the search box to look for just that kind of result.
Press and hold a notification in the Action Center to mute its app for an hour, eight hours or until morning.
Save your Start as Home, Work or Trip in the Start settings, and put one back with a touch.
The settings have a search of their own: type what you are looking for at the top.
A group title above a row of tiles keeps Start tidy: use the title button in the edit bar.
Type torch, silent or vibrate in the search box to switch it on the spot.
Add a Steps tile and choose your daily goal in the Start settings.
Add a Parked car tile and press the button when you leave the car: it shows the way back.
Lock the layout in the Start settings so a tile never moves by mistake.
Start lower down brings the tiles under your thumb when you use the phone with one hand.
A Recorder tile keeps your voice notes: rename them and send them from its page.
The Action Center can show volume presets: save the volumes you like under a name.
The flashlight can put itself out after a few minutes: choose how long in the Action Center settings.
Press and hold a button in the top row of the Action Center settings and drag it to another place.
A tile can take the colour of its icon instead of the accent: see the icon settings.
Choose round or rounded icons in the icon settings.
The accent colour can be different at night: see the Start and theme settings.
The weather page shows the rain, the air, the pollen and more: choose what you want to see in the live tiles settings.
Keep several copies of your backup in the folder, and restore only Start, the settings or the look.
Undo can go back more than one change to Start: choose how many in the Start settings.

Clear when the app is opened

Opening the app from Start or the app list takes away its notifications and the number on its tile. They stay in the history of the Action Center for a while. Opening the app from elsewhere (its notification, the recent apps) does not.
